verdicts.question: Is the building currently under construction?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 9-10: steel scaffolding erected along the side of the building, bare cement-plastered (unpainted) lower walls, construction debris, broken blocks and loose soil in the setback. Page 6: stacked precast fence panels and rubble on side path. Page 10 meter box: loose unterminated wires hanging out. Page 5: front facade is finished but construction material lies near the entrance.
verdicts.rationale: Multiple photos (p6, p9, p10) show clear under-construction indicators (scaffolding, unfinished plaster, debris, unterminated wiring); consistent with 'Yes'.

verdicts.question: In an under-construction building, are existing conduit pipes available for AC, DC cables, and earthing?
verdicts.designer_notes: All the cables in connection with this system execution have to be laid separately, following the given cable routing.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7: inverter room walls freshly plastered with no visible conduit stubs/outlets; cable routes drawn as new surface runs. Page 8: caption says cables to be taken out by drilling holes in the wall; route drawn along the wall to a new MCB box near the main meter. Page 9: AC earthing cable to exit through the wall behind the door.
verdicts.rationale: Photos are consistent with no conduits (new drilled penetrations planned, no conduit ends visible), but embedded conduits cannot be ruled out visually. Absence cannot be proven from photos.

verdicts.question: What is the height of the building and how many floors does it have?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5 Building Exterior: ground floor (stilt/parking + main entrance with steps), first floor with glass-railed balcony, second floor with cantilevered roof slab on top. No visible headroom/upper structure above. Side views (p6, p9) also show 3 storeys of windows. Three storeys at ~3-3.3m each ~= 10m.
verdicts.rationale: Exterior clearly shows G+2; designer's 10m (G+2) is consistent.

verdicts.question: Is the site photo matching with the building description?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5 shows a G+2 residential villa matching 'Villa 64, DSR Elixir' residential description; side/rear photos (p6, p9, p10) show the same cream-plastered building with matching window style.
verdicts.rationale: Building exterior and side photos are consistent with each other and with the G+2 residential villa description.

verdicts.question: Is there an overhead HT line passing within a 10-meter radius of the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5 Building Exterior: a single thin overhead wire crosses the sky diagonally just above the roof level in front of the building. It looks like a light service/telecom cable (single conductor, no insulator strings or HT poles visible), but its source and voltage cannot be confirmed. No rooftop photos exist to check surroundings at roof level.
verdicts.rationale: An overhead conductor is visible near the roofline; it does not look like an HT line, but this cannot be confirmed from the photo. Reviewer should confirm what the wire is and its distance from the roof.

verdicts.question: Can the delivery van/truck reach the material unloading point?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 5 Building Exterior / Material Delivery Route: wide paved forecourt/driveway directly in front of the building with open access; route arrow drawn from forecourt to left side of the building.
verdicts.rationale: Open paved approach to the front of the building supports vehicle access to the unloading point.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstacles at the site that could hinder material lifting?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 6: route along the left side passes over loose soil, rubble, broken concrete and stacked precast fence panels. Pages 9-10: scaffolding and debris in the side setback. No photos of the roof, staircase or lifting path to the roof are included (all roof questions answered N/A).
verdicts.rationale: Ground-level route has construction debris that may hinder movement, and the lifting path to the roof (for 20 kWp of modules) is not documented. Cannot confirm 'No obstacles'.

verdicts.question: Where will the Inverter, DCDB, ACDB, Battery, etc. be located?
verdicts.designer_answer: All the equipment can be installed inside the room allocated for the inverter and batteries on the ground floor.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 6 (lower photo): ground-level door at grade on the side of the building leading into the room. Page 7 'Inverter room with cable routing': small plastered indoor room with tiled floor; overlays mark INVERTER, Fuse box and BATTERY-3 Nos. on the back wall. Second photo on p7 shows a sloping ceiling (room appears to be under a staircase).
verdicts.rationale: Photos show a dedicated ground-floor indoor room with the inverter, fuse box and 3 batteries marked; matches the answer. Note: the room is narrow with a sloped ceiling, so check clearances for 3 batteries plus a 20 kW inverter.

verdicts.question: Is a canopy required for protecting the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7: equipment is proposed inside an enclosed indoor room with plastered walls, ceiling and tiled floor.
verdicts.rationale: Indoor location means no canopy is needed; consistent with 'No'.

verdicts.question: Did you discuss the location of the earth pits with the customer?
verdicts.designer_notes: The setback ground is available on the northwest side of the building (near the inverter room)
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 9 (lower): 'AC Earth Pit' marker placed on the soil setback directly opposite the inverter room door, with the earthing route drawn from the wall. Page 10 'Earth Pit Location': long open soil strip between the building and the boundary wall. Only the AC earth pit is marked; DC and LA pit locations are not marked although they appear in the legend. Compass direction (northwest) cannot be checked from the photos.
verdicts.rationale: A specific earth-pit location next to the inverter room is documented in the photos, which supports the answer. Whether it was discussed with the customer, and the NW orientation, cannot be verified visually. DC/LA pit locations are not marked.

verdicts.question: What's the inverter location decided with the client in case of String/SolarEdge/Hybrid?
verdicts.designer_answer: All the equipment can be installed inside the room allocated for the inverter and batteries on the ground floor.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7: INVERTER overlay on the back wall of the ground-floor inverter/battery room, beside the Fuse box and above BATTERY-3 Nos.
verdicts.rationale: Inverter position is clearly marked in the ground-floor room; consistent with the answer.

verdicts.question: Where is the Internet Router located?
verdicts.designer_answer: Currently under construction. Internet router will be provided at the inverter location by the customer.
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 7 and 9: the inverter room is bare (plastered walls, no network point, no router, no data cabling visible). The building shows under-construction indicators.
verdicts.rationale: No router or network infrastructure is visible yet, which is consistent with the 'under construction / to be provided by the customer' answer. The future provision cannot be verified.

verdicts.question: What's the Wi-Fi strength of the router near to the String inverter/Envoy?
verdicts.photo_observation: No router or Wi-Fi equipment is visible in any photo; the inverter room is bare and unfinished.
verdicts.rationale: Consistent with Wi-Fi not yet being available at an under-construction site.

verdicts.question: Did you pin the site location in your WhatsApp when you were at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Not visually verifiable from photos. Page 1 has GPS coordinates (13.02876, 77.74181) and a Google Maps link.
verdicts.rationale: A WhatsApp location pin cannot be verified from TSVR photos. GPS coordinates are present in the report, but the reviewer must confirm the WhatsApp pin.

verdicts.question: What type of energy meter is currently installed?
verdicts.designer_notes: Building under construction. A 3-phase meter box is available, but no meter is fixed yet.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 10 'Meter Box': two-compartment metal meter cubicle with doors open. Left compartment has a 'MAIN METER' placeholder overlay, three porcelain fuse carriers (kit-kat style, consistent with 3-phase incoming) and a neutral link at the bottom, with loose red/yellow/blue/black conductors where a meter would be. Right compartment has a DIN rail with an MCB and many loose wires. Multiple unterminated wires hang below the box. No physical energy meter is visible (the overlay may hide part of the area).
verdicts.rationale: Three-phase meter box (3 fuse carriers, R/Y/B conductors) with no meter installed matches the designer's note. The overlay partly hides the meter mounting area.

verdicts.question: Is the Meter cubicle photo matching with the previous answer?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 10 'Meter Box' shows a 3-phase meter cubicle (3 fuse carriers, R/Y/B wiring) with loose, unterminated conductors and no meter fitted.
verdicts.rationale: The meter cubicle photo is consistent with 'a 3-phase meter box is available, but no meter is fixed yet'.

verdicts.question: Has the termination point in the Main meter panel been identified?
verdicts.designer_notes: Building under construction. A 3-phase meter box is available, but no meter is fixed yet.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 10: meter box has no meter and loose wiring, so there is no defined termination point inside the main meter panel. Page 8 (lower): caption says 'termination of Input/Output cables at separate 4P, 40A MCBs at the box near the main meter', and overlays show 'MAIN METER' and 'Input/Output MCB box' on the wall beside it.
verdicts.rationale: 'No' (inside the main meter panel) fits the empty, unwired meter box. But page 8 documents a planned termination at a separate 4P 40A MCB box next to the main meter, which reads as a termination point having been identified. The reviewer should reconcile the answer with the page 8 plan.

verdicts.question: In Main meter panel, is empty space available for solar meter?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 10: both compartments of the meter cubicle are taken (left = main meter position with fuse carriers/neutral link; right = DIN rail with MCB and dense wiring). No spare compartment is visible.
verdicts.rationale: Neither compartment has visible spare space for a solar meter; consistent with 'No'.

verdicts.question: Is there space available to dig DC, AC and LA earth pits?
verdicts.designer_notes: The setback ground is available on the northwest side of the building (near the inverter room)
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 9 and 10: long unpaved soil setback strip between the building side wall and the compound wall, roughly 1-1.5 m wide and many metres long, adjacent to the inverter room door. 'AC Earth Pit' is marked there on p9.
verdicts.rationale: Clear open soil area next to the inverter room is suitable for the earth pits. NW orientation cannot be verified from the photos.

verdicts.question: What type of Earthing chamber needs to be installed at site? Is it Cement chamber or PVC chamber?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 9-10: earth pit area is bare soil in a side setback. Nothing in the photos dictates the chamber type (no paving, no vehicular area over the pit location).
verdicts.rationale: Chamber type is a design choice that the photos cannot confirm. A PVC chamber is plausible for an unpaved setback.

verdicts.question: Are there any challenges with respect to Installation and Maintenance activities?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 6, 9, 10: active construction site with scaffolding, debris and uneven ground along the access path. Page 7: inverter room is narrow with a sloped (under-stair) ceiling. No roof photos are provided to judge module installation/maintenance access.
verdicts.rationale: Site conditions (construction debris, narrow sloped-ceiling equipment room, undocumented roof) mean installation and maintenance challenges cannot be ruled out from the photos.

verdicts.question: Are there any safety risks associated with accessing the roof for installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: No rooftop, parapet, staircase or roof-access photos are included in the TSVR (all roof-detail questions answered N/A). Pages 9-10 show scaffolding on the side of the building.
verdicts.rationale: Roof access, parapet height and edge protection are not documented, so the 'No safety risk' answer cannot be verified.

verdicts.question: Is ventilation available in the battery location?
verdicts.designer_notes: Currently there is no ventillation given. But the provision for ventilation will be provided by the customer.
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7 (both photos) and page 9 (upper): the inverter/battery room shows plain plastered walls with no window, louvre or exhaust opening; the only opening is the external door. The ceiling slopes (under-stair space).
verdicts.rationale: No ventilation openings are visible in the room photos; consistent with 'No'. Customer scope item 3 on page 11 also requires the customer to add ventilation.

verdicts.question: Is Battery wall mounted or stand mounted?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7: 'BATTERY- 3 Nos.' overlay placed low on the back wall near floor level, below the Fuse box and beside the inverter. This is a planned placement; no stand or battery hardware exists yet.
verdicts.rationale: The overlay position near the floor fits a stand mount, but the mounting method cannot be seen in a photo of an empty room.

verdicts.question: Should the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB be installed on a metal grill or wall mount?
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 7: INVERTER and Fuse box overlays placed directly on the plastered masonry back wall of the indoor room; no metal grill is shown or planned.
verdicts.rationale: Indoor solid masonry wall location supports wall mounting.

verdicts.question: Provide the dimensions for solar meter cubicle placement (L x W of wall).
verdicts.photo_observation: Page 8 (lower): wall area beside the main meter with a 'MAIN METER' overlay and an 'Input/Output MCB box' overlay; there is wall space around it, but no solar meter location is explicitly marked. Page 10: the meter cubicle has no spare compartment.
verdicts.rationale: No solar meter position is marked, so the 400 x 400 wall space cannot be measured or confirmed from the photos.

verdicts.question: Provide the dimension for earth pits location (L x W of available space).
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 9-10: soil setback strip between the building and the compound wall looks roughly 1-1.5 m wide and well over 5 m long, near the inverter room.
verdicts.rationale: A visual estimate of the setback strip (about 1 m+ wide, more than 5 m long) is consistent with 5000 x 1000 mm. Exact dimensions cannot be measured.

verdicts.question: Is LAN cable under customer scope?
verdicts.photo_observation: Not a visual item. Page 11 Customer Scope item 2: 'Providing an active Wi-Fi or LAN cable connection up to the Enphase Accessories box location.'
verdicts.rationale: The report's customer-scope section confirms LAN/Wi-Fi is under customer scope. Note: the wording mentions an 'Enphase Accessories box' although this is a Deye hybrid system, which looks like boilerplate that needs correcting.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: AC side only: p7 inverter room -> purple input/output route along the floor/wall (4C x 10 sq.mm Cu flex, 2 sets) -> p8 route exits through a drilled wall hole -> runs along an external wall -> 'Input/Output MCB box' beside 'MAIN METER' (4P 40A MCBs). AC earthing (green) p9: through the wall behind the door -> AC Earth Pit in the setback. MISSING: no rooftop/PV array photos, no DC cable route from modules to the inverter, no DC earth pit, no LA cable or LA pit, no solar meter position. All roof-detail questions are N/A. No conduit or clipping is specified for the exposed external run on p8.
verdicts.rationale: The documented AC run is continuous (inverter -> MCB box near main meter) and the AC earthing route is traced. The PV/DC half of the run (rooftop array -> inverter), DC/LA earthing and solar meter are not documented at all, which is unusual for a 20 kWp hybrid. This is missing evidence rather than a contradiction, so it is not a FAIL. The reviewer should get roof/DC routing photos or confirm the PV array scope.
